title: The tunnel envelope
kid: The mobile network makes a private tunnel between the tower and the mobile core. Your parcel keeps the same phone address while the big tunnel envelope changes around it.
nerd: GTP-U carries the UE IP packet through the operator network. The gNB and UPF/PGW use outer IP plus UDP/2152 with a TEID, as specified by 3GPP TS 29.281.

cell-tower.title: The tower opens the tunnel
cell-tower.kid: At the tower, the big tunnel envelope comes off. Your parcel still says 100.64.12.7, so the tower can send it over the radio to your phone.
cell-tower.nerd: On the downlink the gNB terminates the GTP-U leg from the UPF: outer IP 10.20.0.1 → 10.20.0.5, UDP/2152, TEID 0x7. It decapsulates the UE packet for 100.64.12.7 and schedules it onto NR radio. During handover, the core updates the tunnel endpoint and TEID while the UE IP stays anchored.

describe.kid: On the road, the phone, two towers and the mobile core sit beside a thick tunnel. The tower tunnel mouth is highlighted. A big tunnel envelope moves between tower and core. It opens at the tower to show the small parcel and address 100.64.12.7. The handover card bends the tunnel to the next tower.
describe.nerd: The gNB end of the GTP-U tunnel is highlighted on the road, with UDP 2152 and TEID 0x7. The envelope moves between gNB and UPF. It opens at the tower side to expose the UE packet for 100.64.12.7. The handover card moves the tunnel endpoint while the UE IP stays anchored.

mobile-core.title: The core opens the tunnel
mobile-core.kid: At the mobile core, the tunnel envelope opens and your parcel can go on to the internet. Even if you walk to the next tower, your phone keeps the same address.
mobile-core.nerd: On the uplink the UPF/PGW receives GTP-U from the gNB: outer IP 10.20.0.5 → 10.20.0.1, UDP/2152, TEID 0x7. It decapsulates the UE packet (100.64.12.7), applies policy/NAT, and forwards it. In handover, the UPF updates the N3/S1-U tunnel endpoint; the UE IP remains anchored.

describe.kid: On the road, the phone, towers and mobile core sit beside a thick tunnel. The core tunnel mouth is highlighted. A tunnel envelope moves to the core, opens to reveal address 100.64.12.7, then travels back. The handover card keeps the address while the tunnel bends to the next tower.
describe.nerd: The UPF and mobile-core end is the highlighted tunnel mouth, tagged with UDP 2152, TEID 0x7 and the UE IP anchor. The GTP-U envelope opens at the core to reveal packet 100.64.12.7. The handover card shows the N3 or S1-U endpoint moving without changing the UE address.
